- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model fails to capture sharp declines, especially after recent spikes.
- Lag in downward corrections: model often delays price drops, especially when sentiment turns negative after a peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon.
- Overshoot after spikes: model frequently forecasts a peak after a spike, then overcorrects downward — true price often stabilizes or rebounds before full drop.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for risk aversion.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum — apply smoothing or decay factor for longer horizons.
